content.title: About
content.content: Egg Burrito with Bacon is a breakfast dish consisting of a soft wheat tortilla wrapped around scrambled eggs, fried bacon, cheese, vegetables, and sometimes salsa. It is popular in Mexican and American cuisine as a quick, filling start to the day.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The burrito originated in Mexico in the early 20th century as a convenient way to carry food on the go.
The combination of eggs and bacon makes the dish high in protein and fat, providing long‑lasting satiety.
In the United States egg burritos are often served in fast‑food restaurants, but traditional recipes include fresh veggies and homemade sauces.
Traditional Mexican burritos usually omit cheese, whereas the American version almost always includes it.
Bacon in a burrito is typically smoked, giving the dish a distinctive aroma and crisp texture.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Eggs and bacon provide high‑quality protein essential for muscle repair and sustained energy.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: Eggs contain vitamin B12, while bacon adds niacin and riboflavin, both important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: Bacon and whole‑grain tortillas contribute a modest amount of iron, needed for oxygen transport in the blood.

items.title: Nutrient‑dense vegetables
items.content: Added tomatoes, onions, and peppers supply vitamin C and antioxidants.

items.title: Satiety support
items.content: The mix of protein, fat, and carbohydrates helps keep you full longer.

items.title: High saturated fat
items.content: Bacon is high in saturated fat, so people with cardiovascular concerns should limit intake.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Bacon is often salty; excess sodium can raise blood pressure.

items.title: Egg allergy
items.content: Individuals allergic to eggs must avoid this dish.

items.title: Calorie dense
items.content: Egg burrito with bacon is relatively high in calories, so portion control is advised for weight‑management diets.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The burrito is usually served hot. Warm it in the microwave or on a skillet, cut it in half, and eat with your hands. Add fresh salsa, guacamole, or sour cream to taste.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Refrigerate a prepared burrito in an airtight container for up to 2 days. For longer storage, freeze it in a freezer‑safe bag for up to 1 month. Reheat to an internal temperature of 75 °C before eating.
